newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares forge ahead on high turnover.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares forge ahead on high turnover.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 5.31 percent on Friday as demand from foreign investors pushed prices higher for the 14th straight day.
Traders predicted the bull run would continue until foreign buying dried up. "Foreigner's are buying at prices that were unimaginable before," said Karmen Cerar at brokerage Potreza.
* The seven share SBI index rose 65.56 points to 1,299.70.
* Six shares rose and 11 fell, while seven were untraded.
* Turnover jumped to 1.1 billion tolars from 799.1 million.
* Bank SKB was the most actively traded share on rumours it may begin listing in London. Turnover reached 607.6 million tolars.
* Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the biggest gainer, firming 9.36 percent to 16,130 tolars.

* Financial consultancies Primofin and Dadas were the leading decliners falling 10 percent each. Dadas at 21,780 tolars and Primofin at 22,230 tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
